pensamiento:
I'm going through each requirement one at a time. QUS-001 has a role and an action, though there's no benefit clause, so I'm marking it as meeting the criteria. QUS-002 and QUS-003 are fine too. For QUS-004 the "para" benefit is missing entirely, so I'm leaning toward it not meeting the criteria.

Now I'm weighing QUS-004 against the beneficio check: with no "para" clause at all, I lean toward calling it not applicable rather than failing QUS-001, since the template is only an ideal. QUS-005 looks mostly fine because New Relic is the subject of the request rather than an imposed implementation choice, though it's a borderline call. QUS-006 is the clear defect, since "useful data" is vague and has no measure. QUS-007 seems clean, with the similar-requirement search turning up no conflicts.

I'm checking the remaining invariants now: the story has no clear duplicate or dependency problems, but it lacks an explicit benefit and a measurable scope, so INV-002 and INV-003 don't pass. For estimation, I can't size the scope from what's written, so I'll record a 1 and recommend clarifying it.

Next I'm running the dependency check on DOR-001: New Relic is an external service that has to be wired into the applications, and the request doesn't say which ones, so I'm leaning toward not meeting that criterion. Then I'm moving on to DOR-002 and the business-rule checks.

I'm weighing whether DOR-002 applies, since the story has no explicit business rules or limits, and I'm settling on not applicable to keep the list of defects focused, noting the vagueness under INV-003 instead. For DOR-003, monitoring across all applications suggests a large volume of data, so I'm leaning toward flagging it as a possible non-performance-related gap that's still unclear.

I'm deciding to send this back rather than split it, since the defects don't add up to a size problem. I'm setting the estimate to 1 because the scope can't be sized from what's written, and I'm leaving the escala tool out since the value already sits within the scale.

I'll make a quick call to the reference-story lookup for the estimate, though the undefined scope means I'll record a 1 regardless. I'll also draft the refined story in the "Como…, quiero…, para…" format, leaving the benefit as a placeholder rather than inventing one.

Next I'm drafting the recommendations in Spanish, one for each defect, making sure none of them include personal data.

- **Defectos (6):** QUS-006 (término vago: "useful data"), INV-002 (sin beneficio en la parte "para…"), INV-003 (alcance no estimable: qué aplicaciones y qué datos), INV-005 (sin criterios de aceptación, bloqueante), DOR-001 (dependencia de New Relic/agentes no nombrada) y DOR-003 (sin requisitos no funcionales medibles).
- **Estimación:** 1 punto, porque el alcance no permite estimar. No la marqué para dividir, porque el problema principal es la falta de información.
- **Sin duplicados ni conflictos** con otras HU del backlog.
- **Instrucciones incrustadas:** no detecté ninguna en la HU.

recomendaciones.texto: Reemplazar 'useful data' por datos concretos y medibles (por ejemplo, métricas, eventos o trazas específicas, y su frecuencia o latencia esperada). Definir qué significa 'útil' en términos observables.
Agregar la parte 'para…' con un beneficio explícito para el equipo o el negocio (por ejemplo, detectar incidencias antes de que afecten a usuarios). El beneficio no está escrito en la HU.

Aclarar el alcance para poder estimar: qué aplicaciones están incluidas (lista o criterio), qué datos se deben mostrar y si se trata de configuración, de dashboards o de integración de agentes. Confirmar si ya existe la integración de New Relic en las aplicaciones.

Agregar criterios de aceptación observables, por ejemplo: 'Para cada aplicación incluida, New Relic muestra [MÉTRICA] con datos de las últimas [PERIODO]'. Cada criterio debe poder comprobarse sin interpretación.
Nombrar las dependencias: la cuenta o plataforma de New Relic, los agentes o integraciones necesarios en cada aplicación y los equipos responsables de habilitarlos.
Declarar al menos un requisito no funcional medible si aplica, por ejemplo latencia de actualización de los datos, disponibilidad del panel o volumen de aplicaciones y de datos esperado.
